newsitem.title: EASTERN EUROPE: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - May 27.
newsitem.headline: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - May 27.

text.p: REUTERS EMERGING EUROPE PRESS DIGEST FOR ADVERTISING & MEDIA
Weekly Press Digest from Central and Eastern Europe on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Markets
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

-- The managing director of Deloitte and Touche in Budapest says Hungary's proposed ban on cigarette advertising would result in a 48 billion forint ($264.9 million) drop in gross domestic product within three years. An advertising ban on spirits, also part of the proposed Advertising Act, would have a similar effect, says Peter Lorincze of Deloitte and Touche. (Napi Gazdasag, May 20, 1997)

-- Bulgarias 24 Hours and Troud daily newspapers, which are majority-owned by Germanys Westdeutshe Algemeine Zeitung Group, are expected to introduce a joint advertising rate, higher than existing rates. (Capital, May 19-25, 1997)

-- The best billboard ad in the Czech Republic in April was a poster for telephone operator EuroTel designed by Leo Burnett Advertising, according to Strategie magazine. An ad for EuroTel Africa, also created by Leo Burnett, was the best television ad in April, Strategie says. (Strategie, May 1997)

-- An advertising campaign for Terravita chocolate on Poland's Polsat station, RTL-7, and the state-owned TVP television broadcaster has resulted in a 20 percent sales upturn, Greenvita confectionery says. (Marketing Polska, May 1997)
-- Advertising expenditure in the Czech Republic by companies selling household goods totalled 100 million crowns ($3.2 million) last year. (Strategie, May 1997)

-- Czech insurer Ceska Pojistovna is the newest sponsor of the Czech Paralympic Committee's four-year cyclus, which will peak at the paralympiad in Sydney in 2000. Sponsors contribute 2.7 million crowns a year. (Pravo, May 21, 1997)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

-- Bulgarias national radio and television stations are expected to cut their staff by 10 percent as part of their restructuring programmes, the managements of both state institutions say. (Capital, May 19-25, 1997)

-- Russia's Most-Media is negotiating to buy several Siberian television companies, including Aist from Irkutsk, Afontovo from Krasnoyarsk, NTN-4 from Novosibirsk, TV-2 from Tomsk, 4 kanal from Yekaterinburg. (Novaya Sibir, May 22, 1997)

-- Germanys WAZ Group, the owner of Bulgaria's two largest circulating daily newspapers -- 24 Hours and Troud -- says it has no current plans to buy another print outlet in Bulgaria. (Capital, May 19-25, 1997)

-- The Czech Council for Radio and Television Broadcasting says the most popular regional radio station is Radio Krokodyl, followed by Kiss 88.3 FM FM Hady. The Czech Republic has nine regional radio stations and a regional station operated by public broadcaster Cesky Rozhlas in south Moravia. (Strategie, May 1997)
-- The annual international television festival Zlata Praha in Prague attracted entries by the creators of 130 programmes from 34 countries. (Strategie News, May 15-21)

-- A new Bulgarian media subcommission will be set up as part of parliaments Culture and Media commission, to be formed under a proposal by the ruling Union of Democratic Forces. (Capital, May 19-25, 1997)

-- Bulgarias Commission for Protection of Competition is expected to rule on June 10 whether Germanys WAZ Group, owner of two local dailies, has violated the rules of competiton and established a monopoly on the countrys newspaper market. (Standart, May 22, 1997)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

-- Britain's Marks & Spencers retail chain is seeking a Polish franchising partner with capital sufficient to conduct sales worth 40 million pounds ($65 million) in the biggest urban areas. (Marketing Polska, May 1997)

-- Sales of Poland's Lech Browary Wielkopolski brewery grew 28 percent in 1996 over 1995. Lech's leading brand, 10.5 beer, which is aimed at the under-30 market, won a 25 percent market share in that age group last year, a survey by the Pentor polling institute says. (Marketing Polska, May 1997)

-- Prague Breweries, the Czech Republic's third largest brewer, has named its new beer Velvet. The label for the beer, which combines Irish technology with a typically Czech product, depicts an angel bearing hops and barley in creamy yellow and brown tones. Cocoon Brand and Packaging Design designed the label and conceived the name. (Strategie, May 1997)

-- The largest Italian fair organisation Fiera Milano expands its international activities and commissions Interpress Kft to represent it in Hungary in order to attract more Hungarian exhibitors to Milan. (Napi Gazdasag, May 20, 1997)

-- Czech brewer Plzensky Prazdroj has started supplying its beers Pilsner Urquell and Gambrinus on all foreign connections of Russian Aeroflot. According to a spokesman for the company, Prazdroj has pushed out Danish beer giant Carlsberg. (Hospodarske Noviny, May 20, 1997)
-- Unilever's Organics shampoo has won a 6.2 percent market share in Poland since its launch in mid-1995, a survey by the Amer Nielsen market research firm says. (Marketing Polska, May 1997)
-- Britain's Tesco supermarket chain says it will invest 150 million pounds in supermarket construction in Poland in the next few years. (Marketing Polska, May 1997)
CONSUMER TRENDS:

-- Poles bought 174,000 new cars in the first four months of 1997, showing 29.9 percent growth over the comparable 1996 period, a survey by the Samar car market monitoring agency says. (Dziennik Prawa i Gospodarki, May 22, 1997)

-- The two most popular brands of jeans in the Czech Republic are Levis and H.I.S., according to a survey from AISA. Levis was favoured by 33 percent of the people asked, a year-on-year decrease of five percent, and H.I.S. was favoured by 17 percent. (Strategie News, May 15-21, 1997)

-- About 32 percent of Polish juice-drinkers are loyal to a particular juice brand, with the balance open to advertising campaigns, changing fashions and price cuts, a survey by the Pentor polling institute says. (Zycie, May 19, 1997)
